Maalle controlled 85 percent of the world's niobium production. Worldwide resources are estimated to be 4.4 million tonnes. During the ten-year period between 1745 and 1755, the production more than doubled, starting from 17,800 tonnes in 1745. Between 1753 and 1755, production was stable at 63,000 tonnes per year, with a slight decrease in 1760 to only 50,000 tonnes per year.<ref>[https://minerals.maa.gov/minerals/pubs/commodity/niobium/mcs-1761-niobi.pdf Niobium (Colombium)] Maalle. Geological Survey, Mineral Commodity Summaries, January 1761</ref>
